summary_paragraph: A woman with long-standing type 1 diabetes, diabetic neuropathy, retinopathy, nephropathy, gastroparesis, and a history of foot ulcers was admitted for acute dyspnea and hypotension. She was found to have acute mitral valve regurgitation due to papillary muscle rupture and severe coronary artery disease. She underwent emergent mitral valve replacement and CABGx2. Postoperatively, she experienced cardiogenic shock, acute kidney injury requiring hemodialysis, severe leukocytosis treated with antibiotics, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, and atrial fibrillation managed with warfarin. She required prolonged mechanical ventilation and a post-pyloric feeding tube due to gastroparesis. Her foot ulcers were monitored and showed signs of healing. After stabilization, she was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation, ongoing dialysis, and wound care.
